Before PS 1.7.8.0 property $smarty ( in classes/pdf/PDF.php) was not declared in the class which is considered as public property.

In this version, apparently, an attempt has been made to clean the code and due to uncertainty, the data type has changed from public to private, which has broken the compatibility.

This problem is clearly seen in the modules that work with the PDF class, and the incompatibility is solved only by changing the type to a state that is available to other classes.

$smarty property should be declared as "public" or at least "protected"

title: Don't check if an invalid address exists over and over again
issue_title: Too many queries to test if address_id exists
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

When there is a product in the cart and I'm not logged in, Prestashop is repeating this query 30 times

    SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE `id_address`  FROM ps_address a  WHERE a.`id_address` = 0 LIMIT 1

Additionally the logic is suspect, because the query does not check if the address is marked as deleted or if it is active. This would be necessary, since the addresses are soft-deleted in the address table.

The screenshot are from Profiling mode on a product page. Checking the individual queries in Stopwatch SQL shows that all queries are exactly the same.

![2021-11-25_161510](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7520695/143466190-ec24be8e-1271-4f87-b7ba-304fa80108d8.jpg)


### Expected behavior

Never check if address with `id_address = 0` exists. It must never exist.
Check only once if an address exists, remember the answer.
Even better: good execution logic would test only once for the existence of the address saved in the cart.

To-do:

- [x] #28321

- [ ]  Investigate the core of the issue to understand: why we are doing so much queries (related to how we store the adress in the cache of the cart) ?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Profiling mode
3. Add a product to your cart
4. Scroll down to query doubles, you'll notice that there is 30x the same query on the table `address`.

title: Avoid using _PS_PRICE_COMPUTE_PRECISION_
issue_title: Problem with orders with amounts without decimals
issue_body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I understand and accept the project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have already [searched in existing issues](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABug) and found no previous report of this bug.

### Describe the bug and add screenshots

When Prestashop is configured so that it does not use decimals, when validating the order with the 'validateOrder' method, the order is marked with payment error (PS_OS_ERROR)

on line 323 the error is thrown
```php
if ($order_status->logable && number_format($cart_total_paid, Context::getContext()->getComputingPrecision()) != number_format($amount_paid, _PS_PRICE_COMPUTE_PRECISION_)) {
    $id_order_state = Configuration::get('PS_OS_ERROR');
}
```

In the if, the amount is validated with the constant _PS_PRICE_COMPUTE_PRECISION_ and the configuration of the currency is not checked. In this case the variable **_$cart_total_paid_** always has a difference with the amount paid (**_number_format($amount_paid, _PS_PRICE_COMPUTE_PRECISION_)_**).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36648048/140820904-b65822bc-b83f-408d-860b-94b7ed222edf.png)


### Expected behavior

The order is marked with the correct status

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install clean Prestashop versión >= 1.7.8.0.
2. Create currency without decimal and set as default.
3. Install the `Payment by check` and enable it or use a payment method that set the status of payment in `payment accepted (ps_order_state id 2)` or `Processing in progress (ps_order_state id 3)`.
3. Create an publish product with price lower than $1000.
4. Create and publish product with price higher than $1000.
5. Buy a product with the `Payment by check` payment method or the one configured with a price less than $ 1000. It should work fine.
6. Purchase product with the `Payment by check` payment method or the one configured with price higher than $1000. This will fail and set order to Payment Error state.
